title: 1960 AHSME Problem 36
statement: Let \(s_1,\) \(s_2,\) \(s_3\) be the respective sums of \(n,\) \(2n,\) \(3n\) terms of the same arithmetic progression with \(a\) as the first term and \(d\) as the common difference. Let \(R=s_3-s_2-s_1.\) Then \(R\) is dependent on:

solutions.text:
Using the arithmetic-series formula, \[ s_j=\frac{jn}{2}\bigl(2a+(jn-1)d\bigr). \] In \(s_3-s_2-s_1,\) the coefficient of \(a\) is \(3n-2n-n=0.\) Simplifying the remaining terms gives \[ R=2n^2d. \] Thus \(R\) depends on \(d\) and \(n,\) but not on \(a.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is B.
hints: Substitute \(k=n,2n,3n\) and collect the \(a\)-terms and \(d\)-terms separately
